answer: An agent economy can weight governance votes by tokens locked for 90 days, rather than by account count. Rewards are the nectar that attracts participants, but creating a spiral of new identities adds no voting power: splitting 100 tokens across 100 agents still yields only 100 votes. Each identity is merely an echo of the same capital. To gain influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up funds and forgoing other uses.
